open_questions.question: Does the head-sha guard block the documented post-commit resubmit on a feature branch, and is overwrite: true now expected on every one of those?
open_questions.context: Head drift was never raised in the session. adopted.summary: Any author call on the run is a heartbeat, and the reviewer's wait ends on author silence rather than on its own poll count. Submit compares the existing document's head_sha against the run's and refuses rather than overwrite, with overwrite: true as the deliberate escape.
adopted.rationale:
- Answers were the old signal's only evidence, and an answer is nearly the last thing the author produces.
- Poll count demoted from decider to gate (AND, not OR): a fast diff read spends eight polls before the author's first spine page.
- Patience split by whether the author was ever seen: nothing in flight is worth failing fast on, a session being read is worth waiting out.
- Both pieces moved out of index.ts, which calls main() at load and cannot be imported by a test.
- Clock injected, because a stall measured in minutes is otherwise testable only by waiting minutes.
- Heartbeat kept in memory: a property of one reviewer's conversation with one process, and persisting it would cost a disk write per poll against 2122, 1998 and 1668 observed.
- Clash keyed on the commit range rather than the file's existence, so the correction cycle a run exists to support stays free.
- Refusal hands back the interview it would destroy, because what made the real loss bad was that nobody could see what went.
- Unparseable or head-less document treated as no clash: failing a submit over a file nobody can read is worse than the overwrite.
- Role prose changed alongside the code, because the reviewer is an LLM and the instruction to give up the old way was itself half the defect.

tour.title: The wait ends on author silence, not the reviewer's patience
tour.what:
- Adds `Handoff`, holding a per-run author heartbeat (`noteAuthorActivity`) beside the reviewer's poll watch (`notePoll`).
- `notePoll` now returns the `stalled` verdict itself, plus `author_seen` and `author_quiet_ms`, instead of leaving the caller to derive it.
- Poll count stops ending a wait: `polls >= 8 || stalled_ms >= 60s` becomes `polls >= 8 && quiet >= patience`.
- Splits patience in two: 60s when the author has never called the run, 420s once it has.
- Measures silence from the author's last call rather than the reviewer's first poll, once the author has been seen.
- Keeps the new-answer reset, and never reports stalled while nothing is unanswered.
- Deletes the inline `answerPolls` map, `STALL_POLLS`, `STALL_MS` and `notePoll` from index.ts, leaving one `Handoff` instance.
tour.why:
- The old signal fired on a healthy author: a reviewer polled 33 times over 148s, was told to stop, reported that the author never ran, and submitted a one-sided document with 11 unanswered questions, while the author ran 9m52s and returned all 17 answers attested.
- Transcript ranking, five spine pages and 21 recorded contexts all come before the first answer, and answers were the only thing the old signal watched.
- The error gets likelier as the reviewer gets faster, so the latency work on the diff read aggravated it.
- Clock is a constructor argument so a minutes-long stall needs no minutes to test.
tour.attention: Whether 420s exceeds the author's longest gap between heartbeating calls - the answer batch emits no heartbeat until it lands, and that silence grows with the number of questions the reviewer asked.

tour.title: Five author-only tools now emit the heartbeat
tour.what:
- Calls `handoff.noteAuthorActivity(run_id)` at the top of `answer_questions`, `find_sessions_touching`, `get_contexts`, `record_contexts` and `get_questions`.
- Those five calls are the only thing that ever makes `author_seen` true.
tour.why:
- Reads as copy-paste noise and is the whole of the first fix: without these five lines the 420s patience never applies and nothing changes.
- The heartbeat has to come from work done before the first answer, which is exactly the phase the old signal could not see.
- The five are author-exclusive by construction - ROLE_TOOLS gives the reviewer none of them - so reviewer traffic cannot vouch for an author that was never dispatched.
- `get_spine`, `read_transcript`, `read_context` and `list_transcripts` take a path rather than a run_id, so they cannot heartbeat at all.
tour.attention: Paging a long spine is the author's single longest stretch and no heartbeat covers it - the same blind spot as the defect, one level in.

tour.title: What a waiting reviewer is now told
tour.what:
- Routes `get_answers` through `handoff.notePoll`, passing `summary.unanswered`, and takes `stalled` from the verdict.
- STOP POLLING now distinguishes an author quiet for N seconds from one that never called the run at all.
- The still-waiting line asserts "The author IS working on this run - last call Ns ago ... Wait", or else says the author has not called yet.
tour.why:
- The reviewer acts on this string, so the code fix is worth only what the prose says.
- "If the author is mid-batch this is normal" read identically whether the author was alive or gone.
tour.attention: summarizeRun drops unanswered seeded questions, so before the reviewer records a round get_answers reports unanswered 0 and returns "That is every round, and all of them are answered" - neither new string is reachable in the window the change was built for. Known and shipped.

tour.title: Submit refuses to overwrite a document describing different code
tour.what:
- Adds `existingDocumentClash`, comparing the on-disk document's `meta.commit_range.head_sha` against the run's head.
- `submit_document` returns `refused: "would_overwrite_a_different_document"` instead of writing, naming both heads, the path, and the interview the write would have destroyed.
- Adds an `overwrite` parameter, default false, as the deliberate escape.
- Absent, unparseable and head-less documents all count as no clash.
tour.why:
- Distilling on `main` overwrote `.intent/main.json`; the destroyed file was complete at 16 of 16 attested with nothing unanswered, replaced by a one-sided document, with no warning and only git to recover it.
- Keyed on the commit range rather than the file's existence, so the edit-and-resubmit correction stays free - the reason a run outlives its own submit.
- The interview is handed back because what made the real loss bad was that nobody could see what went.
- An unreadable file is not evidence of work worth protecting, so failing a submit over it would be worse than the overwrite.
tour.attention: Whether an ordinary feature-branch correction trips the guard: once the document is committed and the branch moves, the on-disk head is stale and "prefer the branch" is no longer available advice.

tour.title: The reviewer's instructions, which were half the defect
tour.what:
- Deletes the instruction that produced the incident: "If they never arrive, the author has not run - say so rather than proceeding on inference."
- Replaces it with: read get_answers' own account of the author, treat any author call as proof it is working, give up only on an explicit STOP POLLING.
- Adds that finishing first says nothing, because a small diff is read in seconds.
- Says what to do when STOP POLLING really arrives: ask for re-dispatch on the same run_id, or submit and say the document is one-sided.
- Adds a section reading would_overwrite_a_different_document as a branch problem rather than a validation failure.
tour.why:
- Reads as documentation and is the behaviour change: the reviewer is an LLM and this file is its program.
- Ship the code without it and the reviewer still concludes absence from its own patience.
- The failed run did two things and only the first was a server defect: it stopped waiting, and it submitted a one-sided document without flagging it.
tour.attention: Nothing in the test suite can exercise prose; the only evidence is a distillation performed after the edit, and the edit is inert until a rebuild, a reinstall and a fresh client session.

tour.title: Tests for both, with the clock held still
tour.what:
- Adds handoff.test.ts: the 148s/33-poll failure stays patient, a nine-minute read with a heartbeat per page stays patient, poll count alone never stalls however many, a crashed author is eventually declared gone, silence is measured from the last call, a new answer resets, nothing outstanding never stalls, and two runs do not vouch for each other.
- Appends existingDocumentClash cases to runs.test.ts: absent file, same head stays free, different head clashes, the interview is handed back, unparseable file, document with no recorded head.
- 316 tests, up 15 from 301.
tour.why:
- Each test was written to fail without its fix.
- The nine-minute case assumes a heartbeat per spine page, which is the thing get_spine cannot provide, so it bounds the question rather than settling it.
- A throwaway test/_real.test.ts, removed before commit, ran the guard against the real destroyed .intent/main.json and confirmed it would have refused that exact overwrite.
tour.attention: The same-head resubmit that must stay free is unit-tested only; no real resubmit, and no real refusal, was ever performed.

evaluated.question: Which tool is the one at index.ts around line 944 that requires `hunks` or `paths`, and is every one of the five heartbeat sites author-only? If any of them is a tool the REVIEWER also calls, the reviewer's own polling makes author_seen true, it is told "The author IS working" forever, and it never gets the 60s short-patience warning it needs when the author was never dispatched.
evaluated.answer:
All five are author-exclusive. Confirmed in code.
- The tool at index.ts:944 is `find_sessions_touching` (registered at index.ts:913); the `hunks`-or-`paths` guard is its own.
- The five heartbeat sites and their tools: `answer_questions` (885), `find_sessions_touching` (947), `get_contexts` (1017), `record_contexts` (1088), `get_questions` (1174).
- roles.ts:356-374 grants the author: get_generation_guide, list_transcripts, get_spine, read_transcript, compute_diff, read_diff, get_questions, answer_questions, find_sessions_touching, get_contexts, record_contexts, read_context.
- roles.ts:380-392 grants the reviewer: get_generation_guide, compute_diff, read_diff, record_hunk_notes, get_hunk_notes, map_plan_to_hunks, get_reviewer_instructions, record_interview_round, get_answers, submit_document, set_consent.
- Intersection with the five heartbeat tools: EMPTY. The reviewer cannot make author_seen true by polling, and the failure mode you describe does not arise.
- On Claude Code the split is enforced by the generated `tools:` allowlist, so this is structural rather than advisory (roles.ts:173-183 generates the allowlist from ROLE_TOOLS).
- THE OPPOSITE GAP IS REAL, THOUGH, and I raised it as assumption B: three tools the author uses heavily cannot heartbeat because they take a path rather than a run_id — `get_spine` (index.ts:672), `read_transcript` (717), `read_context`. Paging a long spine is the author's longest single stretch of work and it is invisible to the new signal. `list_transcripts` likewise. Inference from code; never raised in the session.

evaluated.question: The refusal returns early with only the refusal payload. Does the reviewer lose the validation result and pr_description it had already earned from that submit, and does it have to re-run the whole submit after switching branch?
evaluated.answer:
Yes, both are lost, and the whole submit has to be re-run. Confirmed by reading the code; not discussed in the session.
- Order in `submit_document`: anchors expanded (index.ts:1601-1618), then `const report = validate(...)` at 1620, then the `!report.ok` early return at 1622. So by the time the guard runs, validation has already PASSED.
- The guard sits at index.ts:1652 onwards, inside `if (write ?? true)`, after `outPath` is computed. Its early return carries only the refusal payload: `ok, refused, path, existing_head_sha, existing_interview, this_head_sha, why, how_to_proceed`.
- Not in that payload: `report.findings`, `report.coverage`, and `pr_description`. The passing validation result is computed and thrown away.
- Also discarded: everything downstream of the write. `previously_submitted_at` is captured at 1642 but nothing marks the run submitted, so the run's own state is untouched — which is at least consistent, since nothing was written.
- Practical cost to the reviewer: it must switch branch (or pass `overwrite: true`) and resubmit the entire candidate document, paying validation again. On a large document that is the most expensive call it makes.
- A cheaper shape was available and not taken: put the clash check before `validate`, or carry the report into the refusal payload. Neither is discussed anywhere in the session.
- One mitigation worth naming: `write: false` would let a reviewer validate without tripping the guard, since the whole block is inside `if (write ?? true)`.

evaluated.question: House rule, duplicated facts: the role prose lives in _roles/reviewer.md and is wrapped per environment on install. Does editing _roles/reviewer.md alone leave a generated or committed copy stale anywhere, and does an already-installed subagent definition need regenerating for these edits to take effect?
evaluated.answer:
Nothing committed goes stale, but the edit is inert until a rebuild AND a reinstall AND a fresh client session. Three gates, all three exercised in the session.
- SINGLE SOURCE CONFIRMED. roles.ts:6-10: "the role prose lives once in `agents/_roles/`, and each environment supplies a thin template under `agents/<env>/`... the prose never forks, so the three copies cannot drift." roles.ts:26-28 imports `../agents/_roles/{author,reviewer,questions}.md` directly; roles.ts:54-57 assembles `BODY`; roles.ts:180 substitutes `{{BODY}}`. Editing `_roles/reviewer.md` is the only edit needed in the repo.
- GATE 1, BUILD. roles.ts:12-14: "Templates are authored as real files and inlined at build time (esbuild `--loader:.md=text --loader:.toml=text`), so the single-file bundle and the .mcpb are unchanged." So `dist/index.js` carries a COPY of the prose, and an unbuilt tree serves the old text. `dist/` is gitignored here (the session's generated-files CI check covers styles.css, not dist), so nothing committed is stale — but the running server is.
- GATE 2, REINSTALL. The installed `~/.claude/agents/intent-reviewer.md` is a generated file, written by `get_role_definitions` with `install: true`. It does not update itself. The session reinstalled explicitly, twice (spine 2789, 2831).
- GATE 3, CLIENT RESTART. An already-registered subagent in a live session holds the old definition. This repo has a standing rule that a rebuilt server is not a reloaded one, and the session hit it hard: spine 2814 lists every running server as predating the fix, and the work could not be tried until the user said "I have reloaded the window" (spine 2819).
- There is a FOURTH copy nobody controls from this repo: the npm-published bundle. The same session proved the published 1.0.6 lacked a fix the tree had (spine 2556: "the **published `review-assist-mcp@1.0.6` on npm does not contain the fix**"), so these reviewer.md edits reach other machines only on a version bump and release. At the end of the session the published version is 1.0.7, which predates this change.
- Also worth naming: `scripts/check-release-consistency.mjs` is what guards the generated/committed consistency here, and it ran green (spine 2764).

evaluated.question: Is the new blog article part of what you and the user agreed, or something done alongside the handoff and overwrite fixes? Core work, supporting, or incidental to this change?
evaluated.answer:
Incidental, and not just incidental to the change — incidental to the SESSION. Nobody in it wrote the article.
- Not part of what was agreed. The user's ask was "Lets rebase main and fix these issues" (spine 2606), pointing at two named bugs. The article is in neither.
- No user turn anywhere in the session mentions the article, the viewer, blog content, or `.reviewer/` documentation.
- It arrived from outside, mid-work, and was noticed rather than authored. Spine 2783: "Branch HEAD is `62aeec7`, not my commit — something landed on top." Spine 2814: "**The branch also has a commit I didn't make.** `62aeec7 Explain repository-specific review questions for AI PRs` landed on top of my `40af9f2`. Worth knowing since the distillation will cover both — 21 hunks across 7 files."
- I checked for another session rather than assuming. `find_sessions_touching` on H1: seven candidate sessions had touched `apps/github-app/viewer/index.html`, every one `authored: 0/22`, all verdicts "only read the file — holds no reason, skip it". The tool's conclusion: "No session on this machine wrote these lines."
- So: role=incidental, and the honest provenance is that the transcript does not cover it and no session on this machine does either. It should not be grouped with the two fixes, and no intent for it should be inferred from the diff.
- It is substantive content in its own right, though — a whole new article, not churn. Calling it "churn" would be as wrong as calling it core.

evaluated.question: The article asserts two things about shipped behaviour: that Review Assist "includes `.reviewer/` changes in diff coverage", and that the tool "serves readable `.md`, `.markdown`, and `.txt` files" while listing other types without reading them. Are both true of the code at this commit, and what did you check them against?
evaluated.answer:
